## Overview

This document fits geostatistical models at the **CSI (centre de santé intégré) level** as a robustness check and comparison to the grappe-level analysis in `02A`. The CSI is the health facility catchment area: aggregating outcomes to this level reduces spatial resolution but may better reflect the administrative scale at which surveillance and interventions operate.

Because the CSI-level data are aggregated **across treatment arms** (individual grappes within a CSI can be in either arm), the CSI-level models fit here do **not include a treatment term**. They model the overall mortality surface to characterize spatial correlation structure, not to estimate a causal treatment effect.

The document:

1. Aggregates grappe-level data to CSI level (summing deaths and person-years, centroiding GPS coordinates).
2. Describes the distribution of grappes per CSI and treatment balance.
3. Maps the spatial layout of grappes, CSI centroids, and Voronoi catchment areas.
4. Fits simple and generalized kriging models at the CSI level and compares them.
5. Generates and maps a predicted mortality surface from the CSI-level models.

```{r Load packages and config}
source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))
source(here::here("analysis", "0-functions.R"))

```

```{r Load data}

# Load grappe-level mortality data
grappe_mort_data_raw <- readRDS(here("data","grappe_mortality_data.rds"))

niger_adm2_sub <- readRDS(here("data", "niger_adm2_sub.rds"))
boxgrid <- readRDS(here("data", "boxgrid.rds"))

```

---

## CSI-level data preparation

Grappe-level data are collapsed to CSI level by summing deaths and person-years across all grappes within each CSI (regardless of treatment arm). CSI geographic location is approximated by the mean centroid of constituent grappes. Coordinates are projected to UTM for distance-based spatial operations.

Note: the CSI-level dataset (`csi_dat`) has no `isTreated_child` column. Treatment arm information is irrelevant at this level of aggregation since a single CSI can contain both treated and control grappes.

```{r prep csi data}

# Mean centroid of grappes within each CSI as the CSI's approximate location
csi_centroids <- grappe_mort_data_raw %>%
    group_by(csi) %>%
    summarise(lon = mean(lon), lat = mean(lat))

# District membership for each CSI (one row per CSI)
csi_dist <- grappe_mort_data_raw %>%
  dplyr::select(district, csi) %>%
  distinct()

# Aggregate outcomes to CSI level: sum deaths, person-years, and lost-to-follow-up
# across all grappes within each CSI, irrespective of treatment arm
csi_dat <- grappe_mort_data_raw %>%
    group_by(csi) %>%
    summarise(across(c(starts_with("n_"), starts_with("pt_year"), starts_with("lost")), sum)) %>%
    left_join(csi_centroids, by = "csi") %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = global_crs) %>%
    st_transform(proj_crs) %>%
    mutate(lon = st_coordinates(.)[,1], lat = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
    left_join(csi_dist, by = "csi")

saveRDS(csi_dat, here("data", "csi_dat.rds"))

```

---

## Distribution of grappes per CSI

The histograms below summarise how grappes are distributed across CSIs. Key questions: Are some CSIs much larger than others? Is treatment roughly balanced within each CSI (as expected under cluster randomization)?

```{r csi-histogram}

csi_summ_arm <- grappe_mort_data_raw %>%
  group_by(isTreated_child, csi) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

csi_summ_wide <- csi_summ_arm %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = isTreated_child, values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "n_") %>%
  mutate(total = n_Control + n_Treatment,
  prop_treated = n_Treatment / total)

hist1 <- ggplot(csi_summ_wide, aes(x = total)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(x = "Total number of grappes per CSI",
       y = "Count of CSIs")

hist2 <- ggplot(csi_summ_arm, aes(x = n, fill = factor(isTreated_child))) +
  geom_histogram() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  facet_wrap(~ isTreated_child, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Total number of grappes per CSI",
       y = "Count of CSIs") +
  guides(fill = "none")

hist3 <- ggplot(csi_summ_wide, aes(x = prop_treated)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "steelblue") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(x = "Proportion of treated grappes per CSI",
       y = "Count of CSIs")

(hist1 / hist3) | hist2

ggsave(here("results", "figs", "csi_histograms.png"),
       bg = "white", width = 10, height = 6)
```

Left panels in steel blue show the distribution of the total number of grappes per CSI (top) and the proportion of treated grappes per CSI (bottom). The right panels show the distribution of the number of grappes per CSI separately for control and treatment grappes per CSI.

---

## Spatial layout of CSIs and grappes

Three maps characterize the spatial structure of the CSI-level data: grappe locations colored by CSI assignment; Voronoi tessellation from CSI centroids (an approximation of each CSI's spatial catchment); and CSI centroid locations only.

```{r csi-map, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

# sf + projected CRS
grappes_sf <- grappe_mort_data_raw %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = global_crs) %>%
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2])

# Map: grappes colored by CSI assignment

p1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = grappes_sf, aes(color = factor(csi)), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Voronoi tessellation from CSI centroids

# create bounding box (slightly expanded to avoid edge clipping)
bbox <- st_bbox(grappes_sf)
bbox_poly <- st_as_sfc(bbox)

csi_centroids_sf <- csi_centroids %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = global_crs)

# Assign CSI IDs via spatial join: each centroid falls within exactly one Voronoi
# polygon, so st_intersects gives a safe one-to-one match regardless of row order
voronoi <- st_voronoi(st_union(csi_centroids_sf), envelope = bbox_poly) %>%
  st_collection_extract("POLYGON") %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_join(csi_centroids_sf) %>%
  st_intersection(niger_adm2_sub)

# Map: CSI centroids + Voronoi + grappes

p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = voronoi, fill = NA, color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = grappes_sf, color = "black", size = 0.6, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = csi_centroids_sf, color = "red", size = 1) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

# Map: CSI approximate locations

p3 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = csi_centroids_sf, color = "black", size = 0.75) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Plot side by side

(p1 | p2 | p3) +
  plot_annotation(title = "CSI approximate locations and spatial coverage")

ggsave(here("results", "figs", "csi_spatial_coverage.png"),
       bg = "white", width = 10, height = 6)
```

The left panel shows the locations of all grappes colored by their CSI "assignment". The middle panel shows the Voronoi tessellation from the CSI centroids, which approximates the spatial coverage of each CSI, along with the locations of the grappes and CSI centroids but is not exact. The right panel shows only the CSI centroids, which are the approximate locations of the CSIs used in this analysis.

---

## CSI-level geostatistical models

Two models are fitted: simple kriging (intercept + Matérn) and generalized kriging (intercept + lat + lon + Matérn). Neither includes a treatment term because CSI-level data are aggregated across arms. The purpose is to characterise the spatial correlation structure of mortality at the CSI scale and compare the Matérn range to the grappe-level estimates from `02A`.

```{r fit csi models}

if(refit_csi_models_flag){

# Simple kriging: Matern spatial RE only (no large-scale trend)
fit_csi <- spaMM::fitme(n_deaths_1to59 ~
                                 1 + Matern(1|lon + lat) +
                                     offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
                                   data = csi_dat,
                                   family = poisson(link = "log"),
                               control.HLfit=list(NbThreads=max(avail_thr, 1L))
                        )

saveRDS(fit_csi, here("data", "fit_csi_simp_krig.rds"))

# Generalized kriging: adds linear lat/lon trend to absorb large-scale gradient
fit_csi_gen <- spaMM::fitme(n_deaths_1to59 ~
                                 1 +
                                lat + lon +
                                 Matern(1|lon + lat) +
                                     offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
                                   data = csi_dat,
                                   family = poisson(link = "log"),
                               control.HLfit=list(NbThreads=max(avail_thr, 1L))
                        )

saveRDS(fit_csi_gen, here("data", "fit_csi_gen_krig.rds"))

} else {
  fit_csi <- readRDS(here("data", "fit_csi_simp_krig.rds"))
  fit_csi_gen <- readRDS(here("data", "fit_csi_gen_krig.rds"))
}

summary(fit_csi)
summary(fit_csi_gen)
```

```{r compare csi models}

AIC(fit_csi)
AIC(fit_csi_gen)

# LRT: note argument order — fit_csi is the simpler (fewer-parameter) model,
# fit_csi_gen is the more complex. 
LRT(fit_csi_gen, fit_csi)

```

The LRT comparing the simple kriging model (fit_csi) to the more complex model with lat/lon fixed effects (fit_csi_gen) has a p-value of `r format(LRT(fit_csi, fit_csi_gen)$basicLRT$p_value, digits = 4)`, indicating that the more complex model fits significantly better than the simple kriging model.

---

## Matérn correlation functions

The Matérn range (distance at which correlation drops to near zero) for each CSI-level model, compared to the grappe-level estimates from `02A`. A larger range at the CSI level would suggest that aggregation smooths over local heterogeneity.

```{r plot csi matern corr}

materncorr_csi_simp <- plot_matern_corr_proj(fit_csi,
                                             "avenir-materncorr-csi_simp_krig",
                                             modelname = "CSI: Simple Kriging")

materncorr_csi_gen <- plot_matern_corr_proj(fit_csi_gen,
                                             "avenir-materncorr-csi_gen_krig",
                                             modelname = "CSI: Gen Kriging")

materncorr_csi_simp + materncorr_csi_gen

ggsave(here("results", "figs" ,"matern_corrs_csi.png"),
       bg = "white", width = 10, height = 5)

```

```{r matern-ranges, echo=FALSE}
# Helper: extract Matern range in km from a fitted spaMM model
# range = 1 / (rho * 1000) where rho is in m^-1
matern_range_km <- function(fit) {
  rho <- fit$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars$`1`$rho
  round(1 / (1000 * rho), 2)
}

# CSI-level ranges (models fitted above)
range_csi_simp <- matern_range_km(fit_csi)
range_csi_gen  <- matern_range_km(fit_csi_gen)

# Grappe-level ranges from 02A (loaded from cached RDS for cross-document comparison)
fitmort_child_gen_krig     <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig.rds"))
fitmort_child_gen_krig_int <- readRDS(here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int.rds"))
range_grappe_gen     <- matern_range_km(fitmort_child_gen_krig)
range_grappe_gen_int <- matern_range_km(fitmort_child_gen_krig_int)
```

The range of the Matérn correlation with the better fitting (generalized kriging) model is `r range_csi_gen` km, which is much smaller than the range of `r range_csi_simp` km for the simple kriging model.

When comparing this CSI-level aggregate analysis to the grappe-level analysis, the CSI-level models have a larger Matérn correlation range (`r range_csi_gen` km for the generalized kriging model) compared to the grappe-level models (range of `r range_grappe_gen` km for the generalized kriging model and `r range_grappe_gen_int` km when we include an interaction with treatment). This suggests that there is more spatial correlation in the grappe-level data than in the CSI-level data, which makes sense given that the grappe-level data has more spatial granularity and may capture more local spatial patterns. However, CSI-level surveillance still captures some spatial correlation, even as it may miss finer-scale spatial details.

---

## Predictions from CSI models

Predictions are obtained at each grid point under the default treatment arm (`tx_group = "Treatment"`, the `get_grid_preds()` default). Because neither CSI model includes `isTreated_child` as a predictor, the `isTreated_child` column created internally by `get_grid_preds()` is passed to the model but has no effect on predictions — the predicted mortality surface is the same regardless of which arm label is used.

```{r predictions from csi models}

csi_models <- list(
  simp_krig = fit_csi,
  gen_krig = fit_csi_gen
)

tic("Get predictions from all models for both treatment groups")
csi_preds_mort <- lapply(csi_models, function(model) {
  # Note: get_grid_preds() sets isTreated_child = "Treatment" (default) internally,
  # but CSI models have no treatment term, so the arm label does not affect predictions
  get_grid_preds(input_grid = boxgrid, spamm_model_fit = model)
})
toc()

csi_preds_long <- bind_rows(csi_preds_mort, .id = "model")

saveRDS(csi_preds_long, here("data", "csi_preds_mort.rds"))

```

---

## Predicted mortality surface

The predictions are rasterized to a regular grid and mapped. The correlation plot at the bottom compares point-level predictions from the simple and generalized kriging models.

```{r rasterize and map csi predictions}

# Drop the isTreated_child column (unused in CSI models, constant = "Treatment")
csi_preds_long <- csi_preds_long %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(isTreated_child))

grouped_csi_preds <- csi_preds_long %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  group_split()

csi_group_keys <- csi_preds_long %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  group_keys()

# Convert each model's predictions to a terra SpatRaster projected to WGS84
csi_results <- purrr::map(grouped_csi_preds, ~
  make_raster_map(.x, proj_crs, global_crs, "pred")
)

names(csi_results) <- csi_group_keys$model
csi_raster_df <- imap_dfr(csi_results, function(res, name) {

  model <- name

  as.data.frame(res, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(
      model = model
    )
})

csi_raster_df$model <- factor(csi_raster_df$model,
levels = c("simp_krig", "gen_krig"),
labels = c("Simple", "Gen"),
ordered = TRUE)

ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = csi_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = pred), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, nrow = 1) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  annotation_scale() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
  axis.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 35),
                      na.value = NA,
                      breaks = seq(0,30,by=10),
                      guide=guide_colorbar(title="Modeled mortality rate (per 1000 person-years)",
                                          title.position = "top",
                                          title.hjust = 0.5,
                                          label.position = "bottom",
                                          label.hjust = 0.5,
                                          barheight=unit(10,"pt"),
                                          barwidth=unit(200,"pt"),
                                          ticks.colour = "white",
                                          ticks.linewidth = 1,
                                          frame.colour = "white")) +
  scale_y_continuous(n.breaks = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(n.breaks = 3)

# Scatter plot comparing simple vs generalized kriging predictions at each grid point
csi_preds_wide <- csi_preds_long %>%
  dplyr::select(c(model, pred, geometry)) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = geometry, names_from = model, values_from = pred)

csi_corr_plot <- ggplot(data = csi_preds_wide, aes(x = gen_krig, y = simp_krig)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_cor(show.legend = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()

csi_corr_plot

```
